title: Genesis: Gantry Implementation
description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
gantry: transparent PATH-shim offload of expensive cargo commands (v1: cargo test) to pluggable remote executors, with cgroup-capped local fallback. Public extraction of the in-house bash cargo/cargo-remote pair.

## Progress
- [x] Phase 0: Repo, docs, contract - COMPLETE
- [ ] Phase 0.5: Walking skeleton
- [ ] Phase 1a: Core loop hardened
- [ ] Phase 1b: Safety rails & explainability
- [ ] Phase 2: Remote contract & template
- [ ] Phase 3: Onboarding, packaging & migration
- [ ] Phase 4: Fleet features (v1.x)

title: Wire end-to-end pipeline and prove cargo test round-trip (exit criterion)
description:
Phase 0.5 walking skeleton, stage 5 of 5 (split from bf-4kw) — the EXIT CRITERION bead. Builds on stages 1-4. Wire them into one pipeline and prove the round-trip. When this bead closes, Phase 0.5 is done and parent bf-4kw can close.

SCOPE:
- src/decision.rs (or main.rs pipeline): when an intercepted subcommand ('test') runs and is not force-local, execute GitGate -> RefPusher -> command backend -> verdict, then exit with the verdict's faithful exit code (Pass -> 0; TestFailure -> nonzero). GANTRY_LOCAL=1 and Tier-0 (no backend) short-circuit to passthrough/local. Crude stderr lines ok ([gantry] decision + verdict trailer).
- Integration test (tests/): a tiny cargo-project fixture with TWO suites — one passing, one failing. Run the real binary AS the `cargo` shim against each and assert it round-trips through the local "remote", returning exit 0 for the passing suite and nonzero for the failing suite.
- rust-toolchain.toml MUST remain pinned at repo root (precondition, already committed in the scaffold — verify it is still present).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (= Phase 0.5 exit criterion):
- A real `cargo test` round-trips through the shim to a local 'remote' and back, returning the correct exit code for BOTH a passing and a failing suite.
- No branch ref on the remote moves during the round-trip (only refs/gantry/* — assert via ls-remote).
- The decision line + verdict trailer print to stderr.
- Quality gates pass ON THE SAME COMMIT: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test (unit + the new integration test).
- On close, parent bf-4kw (umbrella) closes.

Work on branch wip/<worker>/<bead-id>. Use bf (never br) for bead ops. Reference: docs/plan/plan.md (Phase 0.5 exit criterion; Quality gates).

title: Add self-recursion guard to real-binary resolution (shim.rs)
description:
Stage 1.2c of the bf-6d4 walking-skeleton split (split from bf-3pr). Depends on child 2 (resolve_real_binary must exist). Adds the self-recursion guard to src/shim.rs.

SCOPE (src/shim.rs):
- After resolving the real binary (child 2), canonicalize BOTH the resolved target and std::env::current_exe() (the gantry binary) and refuse if they point at the same file — the infinite re-exec guard (plan §1: 'refuse to exec a path whose canonical target is the gantry binary').
- Surface a loud, specific error (e.g. 'gantry would re-exec itself: resolved cargo is the gantry binary; refusing') rather than silently proceeding or looping.
- Canonicalization failures (target missing/unresolvable) are reported as errors too; never a fallback-to-self.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A resolved path whose canonicalized form equals current_exe()'s canonical form is REJECTED (guard fires).
- A distinct real cargo binary passes the guard unchanged.
- Symlink/relative-path indirection that ultimately resolves to the gantry binary is STILL detected (canonical comparison).
- Unit-tested (point the override or PATH at a copy/symlink of current_exe); compiles with config.rs + shim.rs.
- Quality gates on the same commit: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test.

title: Add passthrough exec and exit-code fidelity (shim.rs)
description:
Stage 1.2d of the bf-6d4 walking-skeleton split (split from bf-3pr). Depends on child 3 (resolution + guard must exist). Adds the passthrough fast path to src/shim.rs — closes out the shim module.

SCOPE (src/shim.rs):
- passthrough(cfg: &Config, argv: &[String]) -> ExitCode (plan §shim, the passthrough fast path):
  - Resolve the real binary via child 2+3 (guard enforced); on resolution/guard error, print the loud error and return a non-zero ExitCode (NEVER re-exec self).
  - spawn the resolved real cargo with argv[1..] passed through BYTE-EXACT (INV-5 argv round-trip; never shell-interpolate — S-4).
  - Return ExitCode derived faithfully from the child's status (INV-3 exit-code fidelity): the same exit code the real cargo would have produced.
  - Fast-path budget: no git/network/config-parse work here; target < 5 ms overhead (INV-4). Use std::process::Command; avoid anything that busts the budget.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- passthrough forwards argv[1..] to the real cargo and returns a matching exit code (a subcommand exiting 0 -> ExitCode::SUCCESS; one exiting 42 -> ExitCode::from(42)).
- argv[1..] forwarded byte-exact, including quoted/space/newline args (INV-5) — verified by a unit/property test.
- If the resolved real binary is the gantry binary (guard), passthrough does NOT exec it (no infinite loop) and returns a non-zero code with a clear message.
- main.rs's shim::passthrough(&cfg, argv) call now compiles; end-to-end 'cargo <non-intercepted-subcommand>' forwards to real cargo with matching exit code.
- Quality gates on the same commit: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test.

title: Wire resolve_real_binary() top-level resolver with env-injected tests (shim.rs)
description:
Child 4 of the bf-614q auto-split: the integration piece that chains after child 3 (find_in_path). Stage 1.2b-4. This child PRODUCES resolve_real_binary, which unblocks bf-1m69 (self-recursion guard) and bf-28dv (passthrough).

SCOPE (src/shim.rs): Compose the three helpers (shim_dir, strip_dir_from_path, find_in_path) into the public resolver:
- resolve_real_binary(cfg: &Config) -> Result<PathBuf, String>:
  1. If cfg.real_binary is Some, return Ok(that path) directly with NO PATH search.
  2. Else: shim_dir() then read std::env::var(PATH) then strip_dir_from_path(path, shim_dir) then find_in_path(cargo, stripped). Return its Ok(path) or propagate the Err.
  - Never silently fall through to self or None; a missing cargo on the stripped PATH yields Err.
- Add env-injected integration tests (set PATH via std::env::set_var in the test, restore afterward): (a) cfg.real_binary == Some(/usr/bin/cargo) returns Ok(/usr/bin/cargo); (b) a synthetic PATH containing ONLY the gantry shim dir yields Err, not the gantry binary; (c) a real PATH with a genuine cargo yields Ok(path-to-real-cargo).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (carried from the original bf-614q):
- cfg.real_binary == Some(path) short-circuits and returns Ok(path) with no PATH search.
- With cfg.real_binary == None, the PATH search EXCLUDES the current_exe() dir; a PATH of only the shim dir -> Err (self-recursion prevented at the resolution layer).
- A genuine cargo on PATH -> Ok(real cargo path).
- Unit-tested via env-injected PATH. Compiles with config.rs + the three child helpers. Quality gates same commit: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test.

No exec/spawn; no gate/refs/backend/local/runlog code. Reference: docs/plan/plan.md section 1 line 105. Branch wip/<worker>/<child-id>.

title: Implement command backend with local bash executor and verdict
description:
Phase 0.5 walking skeleton, stage 4 of 5 (split from bf-4kw). Builds on stages 1-3. This stage runs the command "remote"-side (same box, via a bash executor) and turns its exit code into a verdict.

SCOPE:
- src/backend/mod.rs: minimal RemoteBackend trait (submit / stream_logs / wait / describe / cancel). Only submit + wait need real bodies this phase; the rest may be stubbed/panic.
- src/backend/command.rs: command-template backend with HARDCODED submit/logs/wait argv that invoke a local bash executor on the same box (the "remote" for the skeleton). submit -> handle (its stdout); wait exit code -> verdict.
- contrib/gantry-exec.sh: a ~30-line POSIX executor that fetches refs/gantry/<sha> into a temp worktree and runs the argv (e.g. `cargo test`). Faithful-argv guarantees, verdict.json, and the failure taxonomy are Phase 2 (bf-2i1); the skeleton needs only: run the argv, propagate its exit code.
- Verdict ladder minimal for this phase: exit 0 -> Pass; nonzero -> TestFailure. (InfraFailure / gate_failure classification arrives in Phase 1a/2.) Panics allowed on unexpected backend output.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Submitting a run whose executor fixture exits 0 yields verdict Pass; a run whose executor fixture exits nonzero yields verdict TestFailure. No real cargo here — just script fixtures that exit 0 / 1.
- The handle returned by submit is usable by wait().
- Log streaming is best-effort (may print to stderr); wait() is authoritative for the verdict.
- Unit tests exercise both exit-0 and exit-1 executor fixtures through the backend.
- Quality gates on the same commit: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test (unit).

Work on branch wip/<worker>/<bead-id>. Use bf (never br) for bead ops. Reference: docs/plan/plan.md (Component 5: RemoteBackend trait + command backend; remote contract).

title: Implement GitGate happy-path eligibility checks
description:
Phase 0.5 walking skeleton, stage 2 of 5 (split from bf-4kw). Builds on stage 1 (bf-6d4): shim dispatch + Config::hardcoded() exist and the crate compiles standalone. This stage adds the eligibility gate that decides a run MAY go remote.

SCOPE (src/gate.rs):
- GitGate checks IN ORDER, each shelling out to system `git` (no libgit2 — matches predecessor behavior):
  1. inside a work tree (`git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`)
  2. HEAD resolves (`git rev-parse --verify HEAD`)
  3. configured remote exists (`git remote get-url <ci_remote>`, ci_remote from Config)
  4. clean tree (`git status --porcelain` empty)
- Happy path: all four pass -> eligible=true. Crude is fine: a failure on any check MAY panic or return a simple (eligible=false, reason) for now; full per-check reason strings, untracked-file nuance, and topology edge cases are Phase 1a (bf-4zh), NOT here.
- No RunLog, no decision integration yet — just the gate function + tests.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A temp git repo that is committed-clean and has an 'origin' remote passes GitGate (eligible=true).
- A repo with an uncommitted change returns eligible=false with a simple reason.
- No libgit2 dependency anywhere; only `git` subprocess calls.
- Unit tests build a temp repo fixture (tempfile + git init/commit + a local bare remote) and assert both outcomes.
- Quality gates on the same commit: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test (unit).

title: Add strip_dir_from_path() pure PATH filter helper (shim.rs)
description:
Child 2 of the bf-614q auto-split. Chains after child 1 (shim_dir). Stage 1.2b-2.

SCOPE (src/shim.rs): Add a PURE, fs-free helper that removes a target directory from a PATH-style string so a downstream lookup cannot resolve a binary there:
- strip_dir_from_path(path_var: &str, dir: &Path) -> String (or Vec<PathBuf>): split path_var on the OS PATH separator and drop every entry whose Path equals dir, preserving order; re-join with the OS separator if returning a String.
- PURE string/path logic ONLY: no env reads, no fs canonicalization, no current_exe. Takes dir as a parameter so it is independently unit-testable with crafted PATH literals.
- Empty PATH, missing dir, dir at start/middle/end, duplicated dir, and trailing separators must all behave sanely (no spurious empty entries introduced that a downstream lookup could read as CWD).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- strip_dir_from_path with entries /a, /b, /c and dir /b yields /a then /c (entry removed, order preserved).
- Dir absent -> PATH returned effectively unchanged.
- Dir present multiple times -> all occurrences removed.
- Separator hygiene: no spurious leading/trailing/empty entries introduced.
- Unit-tested with crafted PATH literals only (no env, no fs). Compiles standalone. Quality gates same commit: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test.

Reference: docs/plan/plan.md section 1 line 105. Branch wip/<worker>/<child-id>.

SCOPE (src/refs.rs):

- sha is caller-supplied (HEAD at this stage). epoch = a monotonic/time-derived prefix (e.g. unix seconds) — the GC lever from the plan; leases and the GC sweep are Phase 1a (bf-3v5), NOT here.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

- No branch ref (refs/heads/*) on the remote moves — assert via ls-remote before/after (the never-mutate-branch-state promise).
- A push to a nonexistent/unfetchable remote errors loudly (panic allowed in skeleton) rather than silently succeeding.
- Unit tests use a local bare repo as the remote and assert the ref name pattern + that HEAD's branch ref is unchanged.

title: Add find_in_path() cargo lookup helper (shim.rs)
description:
Child 3 of the bf-614q auto-split. Chains after child 2 (strip_dir_from_path). Stage 1.2b-3.

SCOPE (src/shim.rs): Add a helper that finds an executable by name on a given PATH (already shim-stripped by the caller):
- find_in_path(name: &str, path: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, String>: walk the colon-separated PATH left to right; return Ok(first dir/name) that is an existing executable file, or Err(clear message) if none found.
- Use std::fs metadata + is_file; honor the OS PATH separator. No env reads of its own (caller passes the stripped PATH string), no current_exe.
- Return a clear error string naming the binary that was not found; never silently fall back to a default.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Given a PATH pointing at a temp dir that contains an executable file named cargo, returns Ok(that path).
- Given a PATH with no such file, returns Err with a message containing cargo.
- Returns the FIRST matching entry (PATH order respected).
- Skips non-existent dirs and non-executable/non-file entries without erroring.
- Unit-tested against a tempdir (create a fake cargo file); no reliance on the real system cargo. Compiles standalone. Quality gates same commit: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test.

Reference: docs/plan/plan.md section 1 line 105. Branch wip/<worker>/<child-id>.

title: Add real-binary resolution with PATH shim-dir strip (shim.rs)
description:

SCOPE (src/shim.rs):
- resolve_real_binary(cfg: &Config) -> Result<PathBuf, String> (or equivalent), plan §1 'Real-binary resolution':
  - If cfg.real_binary is Some, use that path directly (no PATH search).
  - Else PATH-lookup the real 'cargo', but FIRST STRIP gantry's own shim dir (the directory holding std::env::current_exe()) from the PATH used for the lookup, so the search cannot re-resolve to the gantry shim itself.
- Return a clear error string if no cargo is found on the stripped PATH — never silently fall through to self.
- No exec/spawn yet — this bead only PRODUCES the resolved path. No gate/refs/backend/local/runlog code.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- With cfg.real_binary == Some('/usr/bin/cargo'), resolve_real_binary returns Ok('/usr/bin/cargo') (no PATH search).
- With cfg.real_binary == None, the PATH search EXCLUDES the directory of current_exe(); a synthetic PATH containing ONLY the gantry shim dir yields an error, not the gantry binary.
- A real PATH with a genuine cargo yields Ok(path-to-real-cargo).
- Unit-tested (inject a crafted PATH via env for the test); compiles with config.rs + existing shim.rs.
- Quality gates on the same commit: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test.
